text: A standing **follow-up rule**: a PR touching a folded/amended ADR's implementation area must keep old public-surface counts flat-or-decreasing, or update the owning ADR in place — no new correction docs that leave stale guidance behind. Each architecture slice carries a deletion ledger (old doors deleted/privatized, new concepts, net permanent concepts), and ratchets prevent old-pattern counts from rising. [...] - **Sequencing is actually correct.** My first worry was that the READ slices are all demotions/deletions presupposing a replacement — but #2335 (build the first typed read session) and #2354 (migrate a browser read recipe) are both **closed as of today**. So the build→migrate→delete order is honored; deletions follow landed replacements (NS-M3's "after replacement paths exist"). #2364 even keeps a test proving a typed session still opens. That's the right way to do a clean break.
